references.text: This reference is directly linked to John 9:30 through the logical argument about God's attentiveness: while the healed man in verse 30 points out that God does not hear sinners, he confirms in verse 31 that God hears those who fear Him and do His will.

This is a direct continuation of the man's argument in verse 30. He emphasizes the historical uniqueness of Jesus' miracle (opening the eyes of someone blind from birth) as proof that Jesus must come from God, which is the core of his claim that it is 'remarkable' that they do not know His origin.

The man in verse 25 responds in the same way as in verse 30 by confirming Jesus' identity as a prophet and God's messenger based on the miracle, even though he does not know all the details about Jesus' origin, creating a direct thematic line regarding the witness to the significance of the miracle.

The psalm confirms the theological principle that the man in John 9:30 relies upon: that the Lord opens the eyes of the blind. This is the underlying truth that makes the man's argument about Jesus' miracle valid.
